terra.problem: The explanation is generic, and “I'd stick to what Moses actually says” sounds mildly scolding rather than fatherly.
It equates fortifications with cities being walled in. Fortifications need not be walls.
“Back to the cookie sheet” is an unclear baking comparison that does not connect to the situation.
It says Moses wanted fruit brought back so everyone could see it. The text does not give his reason.
The presence of fruit does not establish that the land cannot also be thorny.
It says the spies show the fruit as proof of their description. The text says they show it, but does not state that purpose.
The passage does not say the people are in a room or that Caleb stands up.
It says the spies brought the fruit to prove the land flowed with milk and honey. The text does not give that reason.
“Tiny bugs, jumping around” is generic filler rather than a useful or funny explanation.
The comparison that a grasshopper is smaller than a sheep is flat and adds little to the explanation.
